column1: # Managed OpenCode model routing consumed by _scripts/render-opencode-profiles.
# Columns: profile, role, model, variant, temperature. A "-" omits the key, so
# a profile states only the knobs its provider actually supports.
# Roles are "default" for the profile's model, "small" for its small_model, and
# one row per agent declared in profiles/_shared/opencode.jsonc or that
# must agree in both directions: a missing or unknown role stops the render.
# The default and small rows carry a model only.
# `variant` is the reasoning knob in OpenCode's AgentConfig. Validate each
# A profile exists for the providers it reaches. That is the whole of what
# separates them: the shared policy, the agents and the roles are identical, so
# a row naming a provider the profile was not created for is the one mistake
# this table can make silently. Most profiles were created for one provider;
# `xing` was created for two, because its two subscriptions are bought
# separately and neither publishes the other's models. The installer fixture
# names each profile's set rather than counting it, so a borrowed row stays
# The Anthropic line mirrors regular's two tiers: the flagship reasons about
# the work, one mid model does all of it. Both tiers moved up one: Fable 5.1
# over plan and build, Opus 5 everywhere else. `claude-fable-5-1` is the
# current Fable — `claude-fable-5` is a separate, older model at the same
# price, not an alias for it. anthropic/* resolves only while the auth plugin
# opencode-go publishes a cheap tier that keeps the million-token window, so
# this profile spends on judgement and not on reading: kimi-k3 orchestrates,
# glm-5.3 writes and reviews, glm-5.3-flash reads. kimi-k3 publishes `max`
# alone, which is why plan and build do not say `xhigh` here.
# `xing` is `go`'s split bought direct: the same two tiers, from the Kimi For
# Coding and Z.AI Coding Plan subscriptions rather than from opencode-go
# reselling them. It is the one profile created for two providers, because
# neither subscription publishes the other's models. Both tiers keep the
# million-token window, so this profile also spends on judgement and not on
# reading. kimi-for-coding/k3 publishes `low`, `high` and `max`, so plan and
# build say `max` here for the same reason they do in `go`.
